audit_findings.title: A one-time fulfillment-network impairment may have been perpetuated through the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.497 billion pretax and $1.908 billion after tax, including a $350 million cash termination payment; mechanically adding the full after-tax charge to the $919.4 million anchor would raise it to $2.8274 billion and the base value from $24.24 to approximately $64.97 per share, before separating cash and recurring components
audit_findings.mechanism: A noncash or nonrecurring charge included in the latest OE becomes part of the anchor and is consequently projected through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of these closures and the automated fulfillment network not meeting operational or financial expectations, in 2025, we recorded impairment and related charges of $2.5 billion, $1.9 billion net of tax.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge and its exceptional nature are demonstrated by the filing, but the supplied record does not demonstrate how the OE ledger treated each component. If the noncash impairment remained in the $919.4 million anchor, the distortion is plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The full-charge sensitivity is not an appropriate correction because it includes the $350 million cash termination payment and potentially other recurring or economic closure costs.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2025 OE calculation line by line; identify the noncash impairment, the $246 million financing and $104 million operating portions of the cash termination payment, other accrued costs, and tax effects; then rerun all scenarios using only the defensible normalization.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $2.873 billion, equal to $4.61 per share and 19.0% of the $15.095 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds the entire cash and short-term-investment balance to operating value as though it were distributable to shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: We actively manage our cash and temporary cash investments in order to internally fund operating activities, support and invest in our core businesses, make scheduled interest and principal payments on our borrowings and return cash to shareholders through cash dividend payments and share repurchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $2.873 billion addition is demonstrated, while the amount actually required for operations is unresolved. Kroger reports a working-capital deficit and says cash funds operations, debt service, commitments and shareholder returns. Consequently, assuming that every dollar is excess could materially overstate equity value.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash using daily liquidity needs, seasonal working capital, restricted or committed balances, near-term debt and settlement payments, and available revolver capacity; rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The unresolved Albertsons claim is an unbridged contingent claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $600 million asserted termination fee, equal to $0.96 per share or 4.0% of the $15.095 billion base equity value, plus unquantified additional damages
audit_findings.mechanism: Any loss not already accrued would reduce equity through a bridge deduction or future OE cash outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: Albertsons seeks payment of a $ 600 termination fee that Albertsons alleges it is owed under the Merger Agreement, as well as additional damages, including expenses paid by Albertsons in connection with the Merger and the lost premium Albertsons alleges is owed to its shareholders, as well as other relief.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuit and requested relief are demonstrated, but neither liability nor a probable loss amount is established. The stated fee alone is below 5% of base equity value, while the unspecified expense and lost-premium claims could make the exposure larger. The record therefore cannot establish overall materiality or a probability-weighted deduction.
audit_findings.action: After the scheduled October 19, 2026 trial or an earlier settlement or updated filing, obtain the claimed-damages schedule, Kroger's accrual, counsel's probability assessment, insurance or indemnification coverage, and any amount already reflected in OE; then model only uncovered incremental exposure.

audit_findings.title: Scheduled opioid payments must be captured either in OE or the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $976 million recorded at May 23, 2026 ($132 million current and $844 million long-term), equal to $1.57 per share or 6.5% of the $15.095 billion base equity value; the January 31, 2026 balance was $1.113 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the expense was largely recognized previously, remaining settlement payments must either reduce forecast OE explicitly or be deducted as a liability in the equity bridge, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the Company recorded $ 132 and $ 981 of the estimated settlement liability in “Other current liabilities” and “Other long-term liabilities,” respectively, in the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets related to these opioid settlements.
audit_findings.explanation: The remaining liability and future cash requirement are demonstrated. What remains unresolved is whether the OE construction embeds the scheduled payments: the valuation discloses no opioid bridge deduction, but historical cash-flow-based OE may already contain a payment run rate. If the forecast excludes the payments while the bridge also ignores the liability, the resulting overstatement is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE ledger to opioid cash payments and liability movements, map the remaining annual payment schedule, and rerun by either modeling the cash outflows in OE or deducting their appropriate bridge value, but not both.

audit_findings.title: Multi-employer pension underfunding may create costs beyond the current contribution run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: Estimated $1.2 billion gross and $942 million net-of-tax share of underfunding; 2025 contributions were $496 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher required contributions would reduce future OE, while a restructuring or market exit could create a separate withdrawal liability ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we estimate our share of the underfunding of multi-employer pension plans to which we contribute was approximately $1.2 billion, $942 million net of tax.
audit_findings.explanation: The $496 million contribution burden is already in reported operations, and the $1.2 billion estimate is expressly not a present Kroger liability. Incremental costs depend on future funding performance, collective bargaining, restructuring or withdrawal decisions. The latest filing also reports declining first-quarter contributions and a $630 million reduction in estimated underfunding, so no current valuation adjustment is demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Monitor plan funding, contribution schedules, expiring collective-bargaining agreements and contemplated market exits; stress only incremental contributions or probable withdrawal liabilities above amounts already embedded in OE.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter conflicts with a subsidiary classified as held for sale
audit_findings.magnitude: Assets with a $275 million carrying amount were written to a filed $225 million fair value, equal to $0.36 per share or 1.5% of the $15.095 billion base equity value; OE contribution and net proceeds are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Continuing to forecast the subsidiary's earnings overstates OE after disposal, while omitting sale proceeds understates the bridge; the net direction depends on both amounts and timing.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 31, 2026, the Company classified a certain subsidiary as held for sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The held-for-sale classification is demonstrated, but the subsidiary, disposal status at the May 23 bridge date, OE contribution and proceeds included in cash are not established. The disclosed asset value alone is modest relative to base equity value, but the unquantified earnings-perimeter mismatch prevents a NOT_MATERIAL conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Identify the subsidiary and closing date, trace its historical OE contribution and any disposal-related costs, verify whether proceeds were already included in May 23 cash, and rerun OE and the bridge on one consistent post-sale perimeter.
